answer: The network caps how much any single account can take per epoch, so even a cleverly large farm cannot monopolize one epoch's rewards — the surplus is spread across many passing identities. The reason this works is that the attacker must pay a real cost on every identity, so scale becomes a liability rather than an advantage. The mechanism therefore aligns self-interest with network health: an attacker gains most by behaving honestly, because that is the only move that scales. Consider a tide as the anchor of the cost.
